title: Post-Course Portfolio: Notes Web App
descriptionMarkdown:
# Notes Web App

## Position in the curriculum

Post-course portfolio: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone. Pair this with the URL Shortener as a second simple Spring Boot project, this time focused on full CRUD plus optimistic locking, rather than a single write-then-redirect flow.

## What is graded, and what is external

This project has a dedicated, automatically-graded checkpoint: **`notes-versioning-checkpoint`** ("Optimistic-locked note store"), a pure in-memory `NoteStore.run(String input)` program implementing exactly the create/update-with-version-check/delete/get core. Passing its hidden tests proves your optimistic-locking rules — a stale version is rejected as `CONFLICT`, never silently overwritten — are correct, independent of any real HTTP or JPA plumbing.

The real Spring Boot service — REST endpoints, a JPA `@Version` field, a minimal browser frontend — is external and self-reviewed against the Required Evidence below.

## Architecture overview

```text
NoteController          <- full CRUD endpoints, DTOs separate from the entity
NoteService              <- your checkpoint logic, reshaped as a Spring bean
Note (JPA entity)        <- id, title, body, @Version version, timestamps
static/index.html + JS   <- minimal frontend calling the REST API directly
```

## Build it as vertical slices

1. **Slice 1 — port the checkpoint logic into a service.** Carry your create/update/delete/get rules into `NoteService`, unit tests unchanged.
2. **Slice 2 — full CRUD REST endpoints.** `POST`, `GET` (list, paginated), `GET /{id}`, `PUT /{id}`, `DELETE /{id}`, each mapped to the correct status code from Chapter 18's semantics table.
3. **Slice 3 — real optimistic locking.** Replace your hand-rolled version check with JPA's `@Version`, and confirm a `PUT` with a stale version produces `409 Conflict` via `OptimisticLockException`, not a silent overwrite.
4. **Slice 4 — pagination and search.** Add a `page`/`size` query parameter and a text-search parameter over title/body.
5. **Slice 5 — a minimal frontend.** Plain HTML/JS listing, creating, editing, and deleting notes, and displaying the server's validation/conflict errors directly rather than a generic failure message.

## Common pitfalls

- **Trusting a client-supplied version blindly.** The whole point of optimistic locking is that the server rejects an update whose version doesn't match current state — verify this with a test that would fail if you accidentally always accepted the client's value.
- **Letting `@Version` silently swallow the conflict as a generic 500.** Add a `@ExceptionHandler` for `OptimisticLockingFailureException` mapping it explicitly to `409`.
- **Building the frontend before the API's error responses are structured and correct.** Test every status code with `curl` first; a frontend built against an unfinished API hides backend bugs behind "it looks fine in the browser."
- **Forgetting pagination stability.** If new notes can be created between page requests, a naive offset-based page can skip or repeat items; document (or fix) this trade-off explicitly.

## How to self-test what the checkpoint cannot reach

- Open the same note in two browser tabs, edit and save one, then attempt to save the other with its now-stale version, and confirm you see a clear conflict message, not data loss.
- Disable JavaScript in the browser and confirm the API alone (via `curl`) still enforces every validation and status-code rule the frontend relies on.
- Create enough notes to span three pages and confirm ordering and page boundaries are stable and correct.

## Required evidence

- Full CRUD integration tests (`@SpringBootTest` or `@WebMvcTest` plus `@DataJpaTest`) covering the happy path and every documented error status.
- A pagination test confirming page size and ordering are correct and stable across pages.
- An optimistic-locking test where a `PUT` using a stale version is rejected with `409`, not silently applied.
- Browser-based manual verification (a short screen recording or a written walkthrough) showing create, edit, delete, and a displayed validation error working end to end through the frontend.
- A `Dockerfile` building a non-root runtime image for the service, per Chapter 25's container discipline.

## Review and completion

A reviewer edits the same note in two open browser tabs, saves one, then tries to save the other, and expects a clear conflict message rather than one edit silently overwriting the other. They also disable JavaScript and confirm the API alone (via curl or an HTTP client) still enforces every validation and status-code rule the frontend was relying on.
learningObjectives: Complete the graded optimistic-locked note store checkpoint and carry its verified logic into a real Spring Data JPA entity
Implement full CRUD with correct HTTP status codes and idempotent PUT semantics
Apply real @Version optimistic locking and map its conflict into a 409 response explicitly
Add pagination and a text search parameter to a list endpoint
Keep server-side validation authoritative regardless of what the frontend does or doesn't check
